wstep: There is no recipe here for syrup made by covering young pine shoots with sugar, without cooking.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to Missouri Poison Center, pine must be told apart from yew: eating yew can cause serious poisoning, because all parts of yew contain toxic taxines.

Herbs, flowers and infusions made from them are not naturally high-acid ingredients; to be canned, they need a tested recipe with an added amount of acid, sugar or both, even when the infusion is strained.
According to Oregon State University Extension, an infusion made from flowers such as dandelions is likely not acidic enough to prevent the growth of pathogens.

akapity: Unlike pine needles, yew needles are softer, flatter and arranged in two rows along the twig.

Although some people use pine needles in food or tea, eating them on purpose is not recommended: some contain volatile oils that can cause nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and diarrhea, and some volatile oils are more hazardous to pregnant women.
JarAtlas has found no checked source for the acidity of young pine shoots.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for pine shoot syrup from a checked source.
These sources speak about herbs and flowers; JarAtlas applies them to pine shoots as a precaution.
